proof:
# Eight triangle fibers: exact oblique critical caps and all their original rows
OC theorem. It certifies the change from the six-fiber step-cap mechanism
to proper oblique critical caps, and treats EVERY ambient normal.

## 1. Exact depth and complete critical cap menu

Let T be a triangle of area one with centroid g and barycentric coordinate
functions lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2. For

    C=[0,7] times T,
    S={0,1,...,7} times T,

the maximum raw mixed halfspace depth is

    Q=112/33.                                          (1)

Its only deepest points are (3,g) and (4,g). At (3,g), the ENTIRE critical
halfspace menu consists of the following three halfspaces:

    H_i={lambda_i(x)-(2/33)(z-3)>=1/3},  i=0,1,2.       (2)

At (4,g) it consists of their reflections:

    J_i={lambda_i(x)+(2/33)(z-4)>=1/3}.                 (3)

All these halfspaces have proper positive-area cuts in EVERY fiber;
no endpoint fiber is fully captured or completely missed. Their own
captured fraction at their deepest source is exactly gamma_2=4/9.
The normalized maximum depth is14/33, strictly above OC's2/9.

The proof of the all-normal lower bound and the COMPLETE menu is given
in Sections2--4 by explicit rational polynomial identities and a finite
nonnegativity certificate. Sections5--6 then compute the natural original
residual program and prove its row inequality for every critical cap.

## 2. Every through-center ambient cap reduces to two scalar parameters

At (3,g), a purely integer through-point cap contains at least four
entire fibers, so has mass at least4>Q; the boundary fiber is included.
For any nonzero continuous normal, normalize the projected triangle
vertex values by ordering them, shifting their centroid to0, and dividing
by minus the lowest value. They then are

    -1, t, 1-t,                   -1<=t<=1/2.

For -1<t<1/2 the upper tail is exactly

    F_t(s)=1                                    for s<=-1,
           1-(s+1)^2/[(t+1)(2-t)]               for -1<=s<=t,
           (1-t-s)^2/[(2-t)(1-2t)]              for t<=s<=1-t,
           0                                    for s>=1-t.       (4)

Indeed the removed low corner or captured high corner is a similar
triangle; its two edge fractions yield the two quadratic expressions.
The endpoint values t=-1,1/2 are the corresponding cone limits. Boundary
lines have area zero in every fiber for a nonzero continuous normal.

The full mass of a through-(3,g) cap is therefore

    G(t,L)=sum_(k=-3)^4 F_t(kL).                         (5)

For L<0, the seven terms indexed by -3,...,3 are unchanged as a group
when L is replaced by |L|, and the remaining term decreases from
F_t(-4|L|) to F_t(4|L|). Thus G(t,L)>=G(t,|L|).
For L>=2 the three negative-base fibers are full and all four positive-
base fibers have zero captured area. Hence G=3+F_t(0)>=31/9>112/33;
the bound F_t(0)>=4/9 follows either directly from(4), or from the
ordinary triangle centroid inequality.

It remains to analyze the rectangle

    -1<=t<=1/2,          0<=L<=2.                        (6)

## 3. Exact certificate in the open projection-parameter strip

Put D(t)=(t+1)(2-t)(1-2t), and define on each branch cell of(4)

    P(t,L)=33D(t)[G(t,L)-112/33].                        (7)

The threshold lines kL=-1, kL=t, kL=1-t for
k=-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4, together with t=0, divide(6) into35 convex rational
polygon cells. Each cell fixes every branch in(4), and P is a polynomial
of total degree at most3 there. Its polynomial can be reconstructed by
summing these contributions for each k, then subtracting112D:

    full:  33D,
    zero:  0,
    lower: 33[D-(kL+1)^2(1-2t)],
    upper: 33(1-t-kL)^2(t+1).                            (8)

On the cell where every term uses the upper quadratic branch there is
a particularly useful exact sum-of-squares identity:

    P=(t+1)[12(11L+t-1)^2+28(t+1)^2].                   (9)

It follows by using sum k=4 and sum k^2=44 in(5). In particular it is
STRICTLY positive whenever -1<t<1/2. At t=-1 its limiting zero identifies
the candidate L=2/11 without assuming a finite Bernstein subdivision
can certify an isolated boundary zero.

The other34 cells are triangulated into42 rational triangles. The complete
rational certificate is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/triangle-eight-fiber-depth-exact-certificate.json`; AppendixA prints
all cell vertices and every coefficient. On a triangle with vertices
A,B,C, substitute (t,L)=A+u(B-A)+v(C-A). If the transformed polynomial
is sum p_ab u^a v^b, its degree3 triangular Bernstein coefficients are

    b_ij=sum_(a<=i,b<=j) p_ab
      binom(i,a)binom(j,b)/[binom(3,a+b)binom(a+b,a)],
                      i,j>=0, i+j<=3.                  (10)

The basis functions
3!/[i!j!(3-i-j)!] u^i v^j(1-u-v)^(3-i-j) are nonnegative on the triangle.
Formula(10) follows by expanding each monomial in this basis. Every one
of the420 coefficients in AppendixA is nonnegative. The coefficient
list is not identically zero on any triangle. In addition, direct
substitution in each listed polynomial gives positive values at every
listed vertex with -1<t<1/2 and at the midpoint of every triangle edge
not contained in t=-1 or t=1/2. Because the edge Bernstein coefficients
are nonnegative, positivity at an edge midpoint implies positivity
throughout its relative interior. These checks prove

    P(t,L)>0 for every -1<t<1/2, 0<=L<=2.               (11)

For completeness the independent verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_triangle_eight_depth_exact_certificate.py` uses ONLY exact
integer and Fraction arithmetic. It reconstructs the branch polynomials
by(8), checks no cell crosses a branch boundary, verifies(9), recomputes
all420 coefficients by(10), and checks the vertex/edge strictness above.
It also checks that each triangle lies in its designated cell, pairwise
triangle intersections have area zero, and their areas sum to the cell
area. The35 cells lie in the rectangle, have pairwise intersections
of area zero and total area3. These finite closed unions therefore cover
the indicated cells and rectangle: otherwise a missing point would have
a relatively open neighborhood of positive area in the complement.
The certificate passes all these exact checks.

Since D(t)>0 on the open strip, (11) proves G(t,L)>112/33 there. This
is an algebraic proof for ALL normals in that strip, not a direction
sample or numerical minimization.

## 4. Endpoint directions and the exact equality menu

At t=-1, the canonical upper tail is F(s)=(2-s)^2/9 between -1 and2.
The successive branch intervals in L and their exact minima are:

| L interval | quadratic coefficients (L^2,L,1) | minimum | attained at |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0,1/3] | (44/9,-16/9,32/9) | 112/33 | 2/11 |
| [1/3,1/2] | (35/9,-28/9,37/9) | 157/45 | 2/5 |
| [1/2,2/3] | (5/3,-20/9,38/9) | 94/27 | 2/3 |
| [2/3,1] | (2/3,-8/9,34/9) | 94/27 | 2/3 |
| [1,2] | (1/9,-4/9,35/9) | 31/9 | 2 |

Beyond2 the value remains31/9. Each row follows by summing the active
quadratics in(4) and minimizing its displayed convex quadratic. Equality
with112/33 consequently holds only at L=2/11.

At t=1/2 the reversed canonical tail is 1-4(s+1)^2/9 between -1 and1/2.
On every branch interval its summed tail is concave in L, so its minimum
is attained at an interval endpoint. The complete finite endpoint table is

| L | 0 | 1/8 | 1/6 | 1/4 | 1/3 | 1/2 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G(1/2,L) | 40/9 | 133/36 | 287/81 | 125/36 | 95/27 | 31/9 | 32/9 |

Beyond1 the value remains32/9. Its minimum is31/9>112/33. These tables
are also checked using Fraction arithmetic by the independent verifier.
They handle the endpoint directions directly, so no boundary-mass or
limit ambiguity remains.

For a negative L, equality could only occur if its positive counterpart
were the unique equality case t=-1, |L|=2/11. In that case the extra terms
F_t(-8/11) and F_t(8/11) are different, with the former strictly larger.
Thus no negative L is critical. The only through-(3,g) equality normals
are exactly the three canonical vertex directions with positive L=2/11.
Their equations in barycentric coordinates are precisely(2).

Any cap containing (3,g) strictly, with a nonzero continuous normal,
has strictly more source-fiber mass than its parallel through-point cap;
its other fiber contributions cannot be smaller. Thus it is not critical.
Pure integer caps were already excluded. This proves the COMPLETE menu
assertion, including arbitrary closed ambient halfspaces. Reflection proves
(3) at the other middle source.

Every point of a nonmiddle fiber has raw depth at most22/9, by an isolating
own-triangle cap on the nearer end side. In a middle fiber, any x!=g has
some barycentric coordinate larger than1/3. Shifting the corresponding
cap(2) or(3) to have boundary through x strictly reduces its source mass
and does not increase any other contribution. Its depth is therefore
strictly less than112/33. The lower bound above and these upper bounds
prove(1) and the claimed two deepest points.

## 5. The natural critical cover and its original convex optimizer

The six caps(2)--(3) cover S. At every z<=3, the H traces have barycentric
threshold at most1/3, so their union covers T. At every z>=4 the same is
true for the J traces. Every cap in this cover is genuinely globally
critical and has the exact budget Q from(1).

For the left source's three caps the captured-volume root at base z is

    a(z)=2(14-z)/33,                  z=0,...,7.

It lies strictly between0 and1 at every one of those bases. Their actual
residual root is

    f(z)=sqrt(1-a(z)^2)>0.                              (12)

The right cap family is the reflection f(7-z). Since f increases with z,
the one-cap residual obstacles are

    e_z=min(f(z),f(7-z))=f(min(z,7-z)).                  (13)

In particular e_3=e_4=c=sqrt(5)/3, and every other obstacle is strictly
smaller than c. Reflection and strict convexity give a unique symmetric
optimizer. Adjacent convexity makes all its heights at least the central
height, so the UNIQUE optimizer is h_z=c for every z.

With s=2c, the unique nearest-neighbor KKT multipliers are

    beta/s=(0,1,3,6,6,3,1,0),
    lambda/s=(0,0,0,4,4,0,0,0).                         (14)

The endpoint stationarity and zero obstacle multipliers away from the
central pair give this triangular-number recurrence exactly. All active
supporting constraints are tight at the constant optimizer, so(14) is
valid for the original program, not an auxiliary replacement.

## 6. Every critical cap obeys the original terminal-row comparison

From source3 the original normalized terminal row is

    theta_z=5/32 for z=0,1,2,3,
    theta_z=3/32 for z=4,5,6,7.                         (15)

Its barycenter is3. For example, substitution in the exact Green equations
with(14), using W_z=(beta_z/s)theta_z, verifies every interior equation and
the endpoint stopping masses; this derives(15) from the ORIGINAL chain.
The source4 row is its reflection.

The residual function(12) extends smoothly to [0,7] and is strictly
concave there:

    f''(z)=-(2/33)^2/[1-a(z)^2]^(3/2)<0.                (16)

Consequently its ORIGINAL row satisfies

    sum_z theta_z f(z)<f(3)=c,                          (17)

by strict Jensen, since all eight probabilities are positive and their
barycenter is3. All three critical caps at source3 have exactly these
fiber masses, and Section4 proves there are no additional critical caps.
Thus(17) applies to EVERY critical cap at that source. Reflection gives
the same conclusion at source4.

In Green form, the positive-beta component is {1,...,6}; every strict
residual fiber is nonempty, and all second differences in that component
are negative by(16). There are no positive empty-residual boundary terms
to compensate. This is the certified mechanism change from the six-fiber
example, whose critical step cap DID cross an empty residual transit node.
Neither calculation is used to infer a corresponding classification for
arbitrary mixed-integer convex bodies.

This is a pending mathematical submission, not an accepted fact. Its definitions, scoped assertions, calculations, and limitations are given in the proposed argument below. A reference to another pending candidate supplies context only; it is not an accepted premise.

# Eight triangle fibers: exact oblique critical caps and all their original rows

OC theorem. It certifies the change from the six-fiber step-cap mechanism
to proper oblique critical caps, and treats EVERY ambient normal.

Sections of the mathematical submission:
- 1. Exact depth and complete critical cap menu
- 2. Every through-center ambient cap reduces to two scalar parameters
- 3. Exact certificate in the open projection-parameter strip
- 4. Endpoint directions and the exact equality menu
- 5. The natural critical cover and its original convex optimizer
- 6. Every critical cap obeys the original terminal-row comparison
- Appendix A. Complete rational certificate
